name: roadmate-backend
description: Backend API server for RoadMate B2B2C Platform

scripts.start: npx prisma migrate deploy && node src/index.js
scripts._comment_sweeper: Phase 1.5: enforces the accept window. A separate process from the API — run both.
scripts._comment_settlement: Phase 1.8: one-shot, run weekly via cron. Safe to re-run.
scripts._comment_billing: HANDOFF §7ter: issues partner subscription invoices past the free trial. One-shot, run daily via cron. Safe to re-run.
scripts._comment_prune: File storage: deletes proof-of-delivery photos past pod_photo_retention_days. One-shot, run daily via cron. Never touches prescriptions.
scripts._comment_config: Writes the client's confirmed commercial decisions into PlatformConfig. Idempotent; re-run after any change.
scripts.test: npm run test:db:setup && npm run test:run
scripts._comment_test_concurrency: test-concurrency=1: every file truncates one shared test DB, so files must not run in parallel
scripts._comment_test_db_wipe: Only needed if the test DB drifts from the migration history. Destructive: drops and rebuilds roadmate_test. Run it by hand, never from `npm test`.
scripts._comment_demo_geo: Dev only. `prisma/seed.js` leaves every shop with no coordinates, closed, and with an empty shelf, so the Customer app finds nothing and looks broken. This places the seeded shops around a point you give it, opens them, stocks them and puts riders on shift: npm run demo:geo -- <lat> <lng>
scripts._comment_demo_offer: Dev only. `demo:geo` and `demo:storefront` build the world; this puts one live 60-second offer in a shop's inbox so the Orders tab can be demonstrated at all. Goes through the real reservation and routing functions, so the offer genuinely expires and reroutes. Re-runnable: npm run demo:offer -- [shop-email]
scripts._comment_demo_storefront: Dev only. `demo:geo` makes the app FIND things; this makes it look like a shop. Categories, banners, collections, ratings, MRPs, and real shops for every industry instead of Automobile only — the platform had zero merchandising rows, so every screen fell through to its empty state at once. Idempotent: npm run demo:storefront -- [lat] [lng]
scripts._comment_demo_address: Dev only. The Customer app takes a delivery pin from the DEVICE'S GPS and nothing else, so you cannot send somebody an address — a client 500 km from the demo world drops a pin and is told 'we don't deliver here yet'. A SAVED address has no such problem: the app lists it and serviceability is computed against it. This writes one onto an account, at coordinates read from where the shops actually are (never hardcoded). npm run demo:address -- <10-digit phone> [label]
scripts._comment_demo_bookings: Dev only, and the third of the demo trio — run it after demo:geo and demo:storefront. `prisma/seed.js` makes six industries and neither gym nor turf is one of them, so the two the client asks for first were missing an industry row, a catalogue, a venue, a shelf and a calendar. This adds all five, per district, including a week of turf hours with evenings priced up and partly booked. ⚠️ It cannot make either BUYABLE: both are prepaid-only by design and need Razorpay keys (test keys are free). Idempotent: npm run demo:bookings
scripts._comment_demo_photos: Dev only, and the missing half of demo:storefront: that script leaves Product.image null on all 49 products and User.coverImageUrl null on every shop, so every product tile and every shop card is a grey placeholder. This uploads a hand-picked photo for each into the client's Cloudinary account and stores THAT url - never the source url, which isOurAsset would reject on the next edit. Needs CLOUDINARY_* set; refuses to write anything without them. Idempotent: npm run demo:photos [-- --force | --dry-run | --credits | --only=<slug> | --products | --shops]
